newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Finance ministry sees Portugal CPI peak in March.
newsitem.headline: Finance ministry sees Portugal CPI peak in March.

text.p: Portugal's inflation rate will peak in March when the rolling 12-month average, the government's benchmark, will reach 3.3 percent against 3.2 percent in January, before easing to hit the targeted 2.5 percent in December, according to a Finance Ministry forecast.
The government's official goal is for inflation of between 2.25 and 2.5 percent in 1997.

The figures are contained in a document, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, drawn up by the ministry's research department for ongoing tripartite talks on employment and the economy with employers and unions.

The National Statistics Institute (INE) announced on Monday that the consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.3 percent month-on-month in January and by 3.3 percent year-on-year, with the rolling average at 3.2 percent.
It is the rolling average that will decide whether Portugal meets inflation targets for entry to the European Union's planned economic and monetary union (EMU).
The ministry predicted that the month-on-month rate would quicken to 0.4 percent in February, when the year-on-year would dip to 3.1 percent and the rolling average remain steady at 3.2 percent.
In March, the month-on-month would ease to 0.3 percent, the year-on-year would remain steady while the rolling average would rise to 3.3 percent.
